canonical_statement: MERIT-HF examined whether metoprolol CR/XL added to standard therapy affected mortality, hospitalization, symptoms, and quality of life in patients with chronic heart failure.
MERIT-HF was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial preceded by a single-blind 2-week placebo run-in.
The trial randomized 3991 patients at 313 sites in 14 countries; recruitment ran from February 14, 1997 through April 14, 1998, and mean follow-up was 1 year.
Randomization used an optimal allocation procedure balancing treatment groups for site and multiple baseline prognostic characteristics.
A five-member Independent Endpoint Committee blinded to treatment status classified clinical events using prespecified definitions.
Primary analyses followed intention-to-treat principles and used log-rank tests for group comparisons and Cox proportional hazards models for relative risks and 95% confidence intervals.
The study was stopped early on October 31, 1998 after the second prespecified interim analysis met and exceeded the predefined efficacy stopping criterion for total mortality.

The randomized population had symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; baseline treatment groups were similar, with mean age about 64 years, mean LVEF 0.28, mostly NYHA class II-III, and 95%-96% receiving an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II blocker.

canonical_statement: Among patients assigned metoprolol CR/XL, the target 200 mg/day dose was reached by 64%, 87% received at least 100 mg/day, and the mean dose was 159 mg/day.
One primary outcome was total mortality.
The second primary outcome was total mortality or all-cause hospitalization, analyzed as time to first event.

Hospitalization was defined as acute-care hospital care lasting at least 24 hours; worsening-heart-failure hospitalization required chart documentation that worsening heart failure was the reason for admission.

population.label: Adults aged 40-80 years with symptomatic chronic heart failure (NYHA II-IV), LVEF <=0.40, stabilized on standard therapy
inclusion_criteria: Symptomatic heart failure for at least 3 months, NYHA class II-IV
Stable clinical condition during the 2-week placebo run-in
exclusion_criteria: Acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 28 days before randomization
Indication or contraindication for beta1-blockade
Severe decompensated heart failure such as pulmonary edema or hypoperfusion
Supine systolic blood pressure <100 mm Hg

exposures.details: Starting dose 25 mg once daily for NYHA II; 12.5 mg once daily recommended for NYHA III-IV; titrated every 2 weeks toward 200 mg/day over 6-8 weeks as tolerated.
Matching placebo with the same titration schedule.

canonical_statement: The study excluded several clinically important groups, including bed-confined severe heart failure, heart failure with ejection fraction above 0.40, and heart failure early after acute myocardial infarction.
The NYHA class IV subgroup was small, producing wide 95% confidence intervals that overlapped those in NYHA classes II and III.
The study was supported by grants from AstraZeneca.
Dr Fagerberg reported receiving an honorarium from AstraZeneca as secretary for the MERIT-HF International Executive and Steering committees.
Dr Wedel reported receiving an honorarium from AstraZeneca as statistician for the study.
Dr Wikstrand was reported to be a senior medical advisor at AstraZeneca.

The authors concluded that once-daily metoprolol CR/XL added to standard therapy improved survival, reduced hospitalization for worsening heart failure, improved heart-failure symptoms, and increased patient well-being.
